smells.finding: The one named seam, is_episode_in_ordinary_search(episode_id), takes a single parameter.

Reduced but not eliminated by this rework. The new membership-predicate seam makes the per-id retirement CHECK genuinely additive at g4. But tracing concretely what g3 would write for 'enumerate non-retired episodes' (SS8), the seam only covers the per-id filter — the BASE ENUMERATION (the glob/scan that produces the candidate episode ids to filter) is left unspecified and is itself layout-dependent, exactly as SS2 explicitly worked out for the sibling id-sequence-derivation case (Option B: one glob over episodes/; Option A: union of episodes/active/*.md and episodes/retired/*.md) but SS7/SS8 do not extend to the retrieval scan. If g3 is built with a naive flat-glob base scan, binding Option A at g4 would still require touching g3's own scan logic (not just swapping the seam's adapter) — a residual, smaller-blast-radius instance of the same root cause the rework was meant to close. See review finding r7.
SS7's several sub-topics (policy, worked example, layout-open declaration, seam definition, single-line-enforcement) are all retirement-themed; the section changes for one cohesive reason.

Two real adapters are named (Option-A directory check, Option-B status check) for a genuinely open decision — per this doc's own Deep-module vocabulary ('one adapter = a hypothetical seam; two = a real one'), naming both is the non-speculative, mandated shape for a decision explicitly held open, not a guess at a future need.
